summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with ejection fraction of 15%, epilepsy, and prior stroke, was admitted with hypotension during dialysis, with a systolic blood pressure of 59. He reported weakness and subjective fever. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, elevated lactate, and anion gap metabolic acidosis. Imaging revealed asymmetric lung opacities suggestive of possible pneumonia or edema. Blood cultures identified Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia, likely from his dialysis line, and stool testing confirmed Clostridioides difficile infection. He was treated in the ICU with IV meropenem and gentamicin locks for the bacteremia, oral vancomycin for C. diff, and azithromycin for possible pneumonia. A midline catheter was placed for antibiotic administration. His blood pressure stabilized, mental status improved, and infection markers resolved. Heart failure medications were held initially and restarted before discharge. He was discharged to an extended care facility on a 14-day course of IV antibiotics and oral vancomycin, with follow-up plans for medication titration and monitoring of a stable complex renal cyst.
